name: Klon Centaur
description: Klon Centaur overdrive (Bill Finnegan, 1994) as drawn on the ElectroSmash 'Klon Centaur Analysis' schematic (ElectroSmash designators). TL072 U1A unity-gain input buffer (R1 10 kΩ, C1 0.1 µF, R2 1 MΩ to Vb); TL072 U1B non-inverting gain stage whose + input is shunted to Vb by one end of gain gang A (wiper on Vb) while the other end, with R10 2 kΩ, sets the − leg (R11 15 kΩ ∥ C7 82 nF to the − input, R12 422 kΩ ∥ C8 390 pF feedback): one gang section raises the input level and the gain together. C9 1 µF and R13 1 kΩ into the two 1N34A germanium diodes to ground, C10 1 µF and R16 47 kΩ into the summing node. Feed-forward network 1 (R7 1.5 kΩ, C16 1 µF to ground, R19 15 kΩ) and network 2 (R5 5.1 kΩ ∥ C4 68 nF, R8 1.5 kΩ and C6 390 nF + R9 1 kΩ to Vb, gain gang B wiper, then R15 22 kΩ + C11 2.2 nF to the diode-side node and R17 27 kΩ ∥ (C12 27 nF + R18 12 kΩ) to the summing node). TL072 U2A inverting summer (R20 392 kΩ ∥ C13 820 pF), TL072 U2B active treble shelf (R21 1.8 kΩ, 10 kΩ treble pot, C14 3.9 nF, R22 = R24 = 100 kΩ, R23 4.7 kΩ), C15 4.7 µF, R25 560 Ω, 10 kΩ output pot. The bypass (always-buffered) path C2 4.7 µF / R3 100 kΩ / R4 560 Ω reaches the output through the 68 kΩ anti-pop resistor R243 even when the effect is on (about 1 dB bleed per ElectroSmash). U1 runs from +9 V/ground, U2 from the MAX1044 charge-pump rails (+16.2 V and −8.6 V as annotated on the ElectroSmash schematic), modelled as Thevenin sources: doubler 18 V / 60 Ω through D7/D8 1N4001 into C21 1 µF, inverter −9 V / 65 Ω into C19 1 µF (pump ripple not modelled). Vb is the R29/R30 27 kΩ divider with C18 47 µF.

sources.title: ElectroSmash, 'Klon Centaur Analysis' (schematic with designators and values, rail annotations +16.2 V / −8.6 V, Vb divider R29/R30 27k, network descriptions, tone-stage formulas, output stage, bypass path). Fetched via the Internet Archive because electrosmash.com did not resolve

controls.label: Gain
controls.note: Dual-gang 100 kΩ linear pot. Gang A (GAIN_A): pin 1 on U1B +, wiper on Vb, pin 3 into R10: clockwise lifts the U1B input shunt and lowers the − leg resistance together. Gang B (GAIN_B): network-2 divider, clockwise moves the wiper to Vb so the clean feed-forward falls as the gain rises. Both parts share this control.

controls.label: Treble
controls.note: 10 kΩ linear pot in the U2B shelf; clockwise moves the wiper to the R21 end (boost, (RV2+R23)/R21 = 8.2x above about 408 Hz)

controls.label: Output
controls.note: 10 kΩ output pot (ElectroSmash: 10K b) after C15 4.7 µF and R25 560 Ω

controls.label: Stereo
controls.note: Catalogue stereo parameter; the circuit is mono, stored only

parts.label: +9 V (battery / adapter)
parts.note: D4 1N4742 12 V zener and C17 47 µF across the jack are omitted (an ideal source makes them inert)

parts.label: MAX1044 doubler, no-load drive (2 × V+)
parts.note: Thevenin model of the charge-pump doubler (TC1044S datasheet Fig. 8/9, MAX1044 Fig. 9/11): ideal 2·V+ = 18 V before the two diodes, which are placed explicitly as D7/D8, so the no-load output is 2·V+ − 2·VF as the datasheets give. The flying capacitor C20 1 µF (CAP+ to the D7/D8 junction) is folded into RPUMP2. Pump ripple (switching at fOSC/2) is not modelled

parts.label: Doubler output resistance
parts.note: TC1044S datasheet (Microchip DS21348A), Positive Voltage Multiplication: source impedance 'approximately 60 Ω' at V+ = 5 V, 10 mA, 10 µF capacitors. unverified for the Klon: it runs V+ = 9 V (lower switch resistance), BOOST tied to V+ (fOSC ×6, lower 1/(fOSC/2·C) term) but 1 µF pump caps (higher term), and the combined doubler+inverter configuration whose source impedances the datasheets call 'somewhat higher' without a number

parts.label: Doubler diode D7 1N4001
parts.note: ElectroSmash drawing: D7 anode on +9 V, cathode on the C20 / D8 junction. In this Thevenin form its anode sees the pump source through RPUMP2 (it carries the same average current as in the real pump)

parts.label: Doubler diode D8 1N4001
parts.note: ElectroSmash drawing: D8 from the D7/C20 junction to the +16.2 V rail

parts.label: MAX1044 inverter, no-load output (−V+)
parts.note: Thevenin model of the charge-pump inverter: ideal −V+ = −9 V (datasheet voltage conversion efficiency 99.9 % typ at no load). The flying capacitor C22 1 µF (CAP+ to CAP−) is folded into RPUMPN. Pump ripple is not modelled

parts.label: Inverter output resistance
parts.note: MAX1044 datasheet (Maxim 19-4667 ICL7660/MAX1044): Output Resistance 65 Ω typ (100 Ω max) at IL = 20 mA, fOSC = 5 kHz, V+ = 5 V, 25 °C, 10 µF capacitors (TC1044S: 60 Ω typ). unverified for the Klon's V+ = 9 V, BOOST = V+, 1 µF capacitors and combined configuration (see RPUMP2)

parts.label: Anti-pop resistor (bypass line to output jack)
parts.note: Labelled R243 on the ElectroSmash drawing (sic). In the effect-on state it bleeds the clean buffered signal into the output; absent on early units per ElectroSmash

parts.label: Gain (gang A)
parts.note: unverified: taper. ElectroSmash and the PCB Guitar Mania BOM give 100k B (linear); orientation inferred from ElectroSmash's description (gang B falls as gang A raises the gain). At gain 0 the wiper sits on pin 1, so U1B + is held at Vb through the pot end resistance and only the feed-forward networks pass signal

parts.label: Gain (gang B)
parts.note: unverified: taper (see GAIN_A); pin 3 on Vb so the clean feed falls clockwise

parts.label: Germanium clipper
parts.note: unverified: the library 1N34A card (IS 0.2 µA, N 1.3, RS 5 Ω) is a generic point-contact fit; Finnegan says 1N34A makers sound different. Reverse leakage (datasheet ~30 µA at 10 V) is not expressible in the diode kind

parts.label: Output
parts.note: unverified: taper; ElectroSmash labels RV3 '10Kb'. Effect-on state: SW1 connects the wiper straight to the jack (R242 68 kΩ across the switch is then shorted and omitted)
